derivation.onset: ICE 6/10 (Grade 2) on Day +4 is the first qualifying finding and is on the record date: 7.7 (section 6.2, 7.7).
derivation.max_grade: Day +7 'opens eyes only when the shoulder is gently shaken' is Grade 3 but lorazepam was given at 12:30, within 24 h (A30, A35), with no clinician attribution: two readings (section 7.5). Reading Grade 3 and reading Grade 2 (from ICE 6/10, which stands independently) are both above the record's Grade 1, so both give 7.2. Per section 7.5/A23 the shared category is used with the lowest proven grade, 2, not 7.5.

ambiguity_notes: Reason would be attribution (sedating benzodiazepine within 24 h of the consciousness finding, A30/A35), but the readings lead to the same category (7.2), so 7.5 is not used (A23 amended, NEW-3). Documented grade is the lowest proven under every reading (2); the other reading is 3. If lorazepam were also taken to invalidate the same-afternoon ICE 5/10, the Day +4 ICE 6/10 still proves Grade 2, so the answer is unchanged. 'ICE not done on 30 Oct ... off the unit' could be read as a documented 'not assessable' statement; it would affect only 7.3 versus 7.4 and the unassessed-period flag, so it does not change this case. Tremor on Day +5 is excluded (4.2).
